clue.text: Watches cheats

definitions.meaning: pocket watches, or the short chains and ribbons they hang from
to fob someone off is to trick or swindle them

explanation.definitionFit: A fob is a pocket timepiece or its chain, and to fob is an old verb for deceiving someone.

clue.text: In storm coaster left with end missing — was it this?

definitions.text: In storm coaster left with end missing — was it this?

indicators.note: a storm tosses things about, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order
the word left loses its final letter, leaving only its first three

explanation.surface: A small cargo ship caught in a gale has lost a section, and the speaker wonders which part went.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end missing' cuts LEFT to LEF; 'In storm' shuffles COASTER plus LEF. The whole clue then asks which part of the battered ship was lost: its front deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The forward deck of a ship, the end most exposed to heavy seas, is the part a storm might tear away.

clue.text: What starts bout with suggestive look at belt

annotationWithheld.why: What starts bout with suggestive look at belt (9): B (starts bout) + AND (with) + LEER (suggestive look) gives BANDLEER; no clue word supplies the O, so the clue as held looks a word short.
annotationWithheld.clue: What starts bout with suggestive look at belt

clue.text: Mean to change special bed

indicators.note: the words special and bed are to be changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to swap a hospital's special bed for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb (to intend), but it is the adjective meaning nasty, and it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Despicable conduct is contemptible and low, the sense of mean as small-minded and nasty.

clue.text: Shifty about bar I have

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for bar is read backwards

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, which is save (all save one)
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A dodgy character hanging around a pub admits ownership of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SAVE into EVAS. 'bar' looks like a pub or a rod, but here it is the preposition meaning except, as save is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shifty avoids straight answers, which is the way an elusive, dodging person behaves.

clue.text: Saw small difficulty about churchman returning

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the short word for difficulty goes round the other piece

parts.note: PROB is a short form of problem, small because it is abbreviated

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for the churchman comes back, read right to left

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, the title of a clergyman

explanation.surface: Someone notices a minor problem concerning a clergyman who has come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the churchman's title backwards, and 'about' wraps the short problem round it. 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see, but it is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same as a short traditional adage.

clue.text: A light plant

definitions.meaning: a collapsible paper lamp of the kind hung at festivals
a garden plant, physalis, whose orange papery husks resemble such lamps

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a paper lamp from the Far East and the physalis plant named after it.

clue.text: Get cheese before last liqueur and smoking pipe

indicators.note: before puts the cheese ahead of the next letter in the answer

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of the word liqueur

explanation.surface: After-dinner instructions: cheese, then a final liqueur and a pipe to smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like the end of a dinner, but 'last' only takes the final R of 'liqueur'. A brier is a tobacco pipe carved from the root of the briar shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Briar root is the classic material for a tobacco pipe, so the wood's name stands for the pipe itself.

clue.text: Take one off seven and it would be!

definitions.text: Take one off seven and it would be!

indicators.note: take one off here means remove a single letter from the word seven, its first

explanation.surface: Simple arithmetic: subtract one from seven and the result has a certain property.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as sums, seven minus one is six, an even number; read as letters, dropping the S from SEVEN leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Six divides by two with nothing left over, which is what being an even number means.

clue.text: With bold opinions go out to make complaint

indicators.note: out means the letters of bold, opinions and go are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Advice to a protester: take your strong views out on the street to air a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BOLD, OPINIONS and GO; 'With' and 'to make' are links. 'complaint' suggests a grievance, but it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint here is an illness or disorder, and septicaemia is such a medical condition.

clue.text: Genuine about name of an organ

indicators.note: about means the word for genuine goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: something genuine is real

explanation.surface: Asking for the true name of a musical instrument or a body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the church instrument; the definition is the adjective 'of an organ', the kidney.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the adjective relating to the kidneys, which are bodily organs.

clue.text: Australian sailor's to start with English

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a crossword sailor; the 's stands for has
a start is an origin or beginning

explanation.surface: An Australian seaman has to begin by speaking English.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aborigine is one of the original inhabitants of Australia, so an Australian native.

clue.text: After first sign of crack decorators lie badly and show false signs of sympathy

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters follow the single opening letter
the first sign of a word is its opening letter, here from crack
badly means the letters of decorators and lie are put into a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Once a crack appears, the painters fib about it and pretend to be sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles the painters and their fib into everything after the opening letter that 'first sign of' takes. 'show' is a link; the surface's pretence of sorrow is the definition itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from the old belief that the reptile weeps while devouring prey: insincere grief.

clue.text: Spy Rebecca behaving oddly in PC world?

indicators.note: behaving oddly says the letters of spy and Rebecca are to be put in a strange order

explanation.surface: A secret agent named Rebecca acts strangely inside a computer shop.
explanation.walkthrough: PC World is a British chain of computer shops; the question mark marks the definition as a playful description of the online realm.
explanation.definitionFit: The virtual realm of computer networks is a world reached through personal computers.

clue.text: What's the point of church?

parts.note: reads as a sceptic's question about religion, but asks for the pointed tower on top of a church building

explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering spire is literally the pointed tip of a church building.

clue.text: Plant flourishing when it turns out mild?

definitions.text: Plant flourishing when it turns out mild?

parts.words: Plant flourishing when it turns out mild?
parts.note: reads as a gardener's remark about weather, but plant means a factory and mild is a dark ale that it produces

explanation.definitionFit: A beer-making factory prospers when it produces mild, the British dark ale.

clue.text: Layer of skin being damaged I simpered

indicators.note: damaged says the letters of I and simpered are broken and put back in another order

explanation.surface: A patient complains coyly about an injured patch of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outermost layer of the skin, over the dermis.

clue.text: Look at the posh car that's going after other vehicles

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
RR stands for Rolls-Royce, the archetypal posh car
that is is abbreviated i.e., and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Someone points out a luxury car overtaking the rest of the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Rolls-Royce) is a crossword convention for a smart car. 'at the' and 'going after' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorries are heavy goods trucks, vehicles of a different kind from a passenger car.

clue.text: Element is returned to the chemist symbolically

definitions.text: Element is returned to the chemist symbolically

parts.words: Element is returned to the chemist symbolically
parts.note: the little word is, written backwards, is the two-letter chemical symbol of the element wanted

explanation.definitionFit: Si is the chemical symbol for this element, so 'is' backwards is how a chemist writes it.

clue.text: Hearing gardener with crop causes jealous greed

parts.note: gardener said aloud sounds like Gardner, the surname of the Hollywood star Ava Gardner
rice is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A gardener overhears talk of the harvest and becomes covetous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' turns 'gardener' into Gardner, whose first name gives AVA; it is not a homophone of the answer itself. 'causes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is extreme greed for wealth, a covetous desire for what others own.

clue.text: Fatty Arbuckle's the first to cast, not second

annotationWithheld.clue: Fatty Arbuckle's the first to cast, not second

clue.text: Fishwife's rival — she's top of the form

definitions.meaning: a school is a group of fish, and a mistress is a rival to a wife, so a fish's other woman
a female teacher in charge of a class, or form

explanation.definitionFit: A woman teacher heads a class, and punningly is the fish school's other woman.

clue.text: Policemen heard in the wood

annotationWithheld.why: Policemen heard in the wood (5): COPS said aloud gives COPSE, but the answer is held as CORSE and the crossing 23-across (held as CARPICCIC, three letters off CAPRICCIO) keeps the R, so the typo cannot be recorded

clue.text: Book individual performers in a show

definitions.meaning: the ... of the Apostles, a book of the New Testament
the separate turns on a variety bill

explanation.definitionFit: The Bible book is called Acts, and variety turns are each called an act.

clue.text: Lively piece of music from the island? Put volume on ten!

annotationWithheld.why: Lively piece of music from the island? Put volume on ten! (9): the wordplay CAPRI + CC + IO gives CAPRICCIO, but the answer is held as CARPICCIC, three letters off, so it cannot be recorded as a typo
annotationWithheld.clue: Lively piece of music from the island? Put volume on ten!

clue.text: Strange graduate's dance

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: An odd university leaver is having a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance with a lively rhythm.

clue.text: It's tasty to restrain with vigour

parts.note: to stem a flow is to hold it back
ginger means energy or spirit

explanation.surface: Something delicious is said to curb high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Stem ginger is preserved young ginger root in syrup, a sweet treat.

clue.text: Man, say, misled when doctor is struck off

indicators.note: a doctor struck off is removed from the register, so the doctor's letters are deleted from misled

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine, stands for a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone was deceived once a physician lost the right to practise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is one example of an island.
